Learn to explain how to talk about where a Swift program starts and how to await from its first line: Top-Level Code, Top-Level Await & Async Main, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Top-Level Code - Statements written directly in main.swift outside any function, which run in order when the program starts.
Top-Level Await - Using await directly in top-level code, with no async function around it.
Async Main - A main entry point marked async, so the whole program can await from its first line.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Top-Level Code, Top-Level Await & Async Main in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Top-Level Code, Top-Level Await, Async Main 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Top-Level Code - Statements written directly in main.swift outside any function, which run in order when the program starts.
한국어: Top-Level Code: main.swift에서 함수 밖에 직접 쓰는 문장들로, 프로그램이 시작될 때 순서대로 실행됨

Top-Level Await - Using await directly in top-level code, with no async function around it.
한국어: Top-Level Await: async 함수로 감싸지 않고 최상위 코드에서 바로 await를 쓰는 것

Async Main - A main entry point marked async, so the whole program can await from its first line.
한국어: Async Main: async로 표시된 main 진입점으로, 프로그램이 첫 줄부터 await를 쓸 수 있게 함

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about using await at the start of a command-line tool, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Top-Level Code, Top-Level Await and Async Main in English?

dialogue.title: Await in the first line

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I am writing a small command-line tool, and I need to call an async function.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do it in main.swift. That file is top-level code, so statements run in order.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. That is top-level await. You do not need an async function around it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It works. But in my other target, I use an `@main` struct, and `await` fails.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then your `main` is not async. Write `static func main() async`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. An async main lets the whole program await from its first line.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oops, I forgot the `static` keyword. Now it works.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Use top-level code for tiny scripts, and an async main for real tools.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And top-level await is only for main.swift?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, it only works in top-level code.
Top-level code is fine for a quick script.
